name: Kelantan
summary_text: Kelantan is the only sub-national unit in Malaysia — and in all of Southeast Asia — that has legislated the state of gender transition itself as a criminal offence. Clause 17 of the Kelantan Syariah Bill passed 12–13 August 2026 makes it an offence for a Muslim to change their own gender, cause another person's gender to be changed, or induce someone to do so, punishable by a fine up to RM3,000, imprisonment up to two years, or both; the Bill also adds 'protection of modesty' decency provisions. The predecessor provision was actually used: in a case reported February 2026, Kelantan recorded its first prosecution for gender transition under Section 18 of the Syariah Criminal Code Enactment (I) 2019 — a trans woman arrested by the state Islamic affairs department (Jaheaik) in an operation targeting a gathering of transgender individuals, heard at the Kota Bharu Syariah Court; the national monitoring group Justice for Sisters states Kelantan is the only state with such a provision. Critically, the Federal Court struck down 16 of 18 provisions of the 2019 Enactment on 9 February 2024 as outside state power; the Kelantan assembly resolved to re-enact them anyway, and did so in August 2026 — deliberate institutional commitment, not a stray provision. A foreign Muslim trans visitor is squarely within the Syariah jurisdiction; a non-Muslim visitor is technically outside it but still exposed to the official climate the sequence creates.

sources.title: Gender change, protection of modesty among provisions in new Kelantan Syariah Bill | The Star
sources.claim_summary: The Star (12 Aug 2026): previews the new Kelantan Syariah Bill replacing the 16 provisions of the 2019 Enactment the Federal Court struck down — including 'protection of modesty' clauses making it an offence for a Muslim to fail to safeguard their private parts (whipping of 3-6 strokes plus fine up to RM5,000 or up to three years) alongside the clause criminalising gender change.

sources.title: Kelantan passes strict new decency rules in Syariah Bill | The Star
sources.claim_summary: The Star (13 Aug 2026): reports the Kelantan assembly passing the strict new decency rules of the Syariah Bill — the enactment replacing the Federal Court–voided 2019 provisions, including the offence of gender change.

sources.title: K'tan trans woman first to be charged over surgery for sex reassignment | Malaysiakini
sources.claim_summary: Malaysiakini (4 Feb 2026): Kelantan's first prosecution for the offence of gender transition under the Syariah Criminal Code Enactment (I) 2019 (gazetted 2020) — a trans woman arrested by the Jaheaik during an operation on a transgender gathering and charged under Section 18 (fine up to RM3,000 or up to two years, or both), heard at the Kota Bharu Syariah Court; Justice for Sisters co-founder: 'Out of all the states, Kelantan is the only one that has this provision.' Believed the first case of its kind nationally, where sex-reassignment surgery is prohibited for Muslims except intersex people.

sources.title: Federal Court rules 16 provisions in Kelantan criminal enactment unconstitutional in Muslim duo's challenge | Malay Mail
sources.claim_summary: Malay Mail (9 Feb 2024): the Federal Court, by an 8-1 majority of a nine-member bench led by Chief Justice Tengku Maimun, struck down 16 of 18 provisions of the Kelantan Shariah Criminal Code Enactment 2019 as beyond the state legislature's power because federal law covers the same offences — the ruling Kelantan later legislated around.
